summary: Oldřich Hujer (1880–1942) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Charles University (Ph.D.) under Josef Zubatý and at Leipzig under August Leskien. He taught at Charles University from 1909 to 1942, becoming ordinary professor in 1924, and at Masaryk University.

Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner (circa 2004–2009) and later held a professorship at the University of Hamburg.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris, Harvard, and Princeton (Ph.D. 1955), later holding professorships at Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard (1969–1990), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1990–1998).
Olha Dobrodum is an Indologist and scholar of religion. She studied at Odesa University in 2015 and has held a post at the State University of Trade and Economics.

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at London Hospital (M.D. circa 1854–1858), he served in the Army Medical Department (1859–1885), as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and as Librarian for the Royal Asiatic Society (1891–1919).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Ceylon and SOAS under William Stede, he became Head of Sanskrit at Ceylon in 1943, later visiting Harvard, Smith College, and Pennsylvania.

Oliver Hellwig works in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. He completed his habilitation under Harry Falk and has held posts at the University of Düsseldorf and the University of Zurich (attested 2024–2025).

Oliver Petersen (born 1961) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang between circa 1983 and 2003 and held a post at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg (attested 2002).

Oliver Philipp Frey is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Vienna, where he served as a predoctoral assistant (2013–2016), and became an SNSF Postdoc.Mobility Fellow at Savitribai Phule Pune University (2023–2025).
Olivia Porter works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her studies at King's College London in 2023 and became a Teaching Fellow at the University of Leeds in 2025.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) was an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and University of Paris, later teaching at Ankara University, the University of Lille, EPHE, and the University of Paris (1960–1974).

Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Pierre L. Lamant. He was affiliated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 1990 and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 2004–2005).

Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Copenhagen, Washington, Harvard, and under Tord Olsson, later holding a post at Lund University (attested 2000–2007).
Olli Littunen is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who completed a BA at Leiden University (2016–2022) and undertook doctoral studies there under Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Olof August Danielsson (1852–1933) was a Swedish linguist and Indologist. Educated at Uppsala University (Ph.D. circa 1880) and under Ernst Windisch, he served at Uppsala University as Docent (1879), professor of Comparative linguistics (1883), and professor of Greek (1891).

Om Prakash is an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma. He taught at Kirori Mal College, the University of Delhi, and the Delhi School of Economics as professor of economic history.

On Shionoya (1878–1962) was a sinologist. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (circa 1899–1902) and the University of Leipzig (circa 1906–1909), later holding a post at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1920 to 1939.
Ondřej Novák (1946–1977) was an Indologist and historian who pursued his higher education at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. there between 1965 and 1975.

Onorio Ferrero de Gubernatis Ventimiglia (1908–1989) was an Indologist who taught Oriental languages and cultures at the National University of San Marcos and at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru (1952–1976).

Oreste Nazari (1866–1923) was an Italian Indologist and linguist who studied under Gaspare Gorresio. He taught at the University of Turin (circa 1898–1923) and served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative history of classical languages at Palermo (1901–1923).
